html:
A town on the Niger where the French built a fort in 1883 and which became the capital of the colony of French Sudan, now Mali, in 1908.

The railway from Dakar made it the colony's link to the sea. It was the birthplace in 1946 of the African Democratic Rally, the main party of French West Africa. After independence it grew from about a hundred thousand people to several million, one of the fastest-growing cities in Africa. Its musicians, among them Ali Farka Toure's contemporaries Salif Keita and Amadou and Mariam, made it a centre of world music.
